name: AI trainer / response evaluator (Outlier)
summary: Scale AI's freelance platform where contributors write, rate and correct AI chatbot answers for hourly pay.
whatYouDo: After a skills screening you are matched to projects where you compare, rate or rewrite AI-generated answers by following detailed guidelines. Generalist projects focus on English writing and content review; specialist projects (coding, math, finance, languages) pay more.
appeal: Official listings name Canada as an eligible location for generalist and specialist roles
Remote and self-scheduled
Weekly payouts via PayPal, Airtm or ACH (official FAQ)
Higher rates for specialist skills such as coding, math or quant finance
watchOuts: Generalist roles open to Canada list 'up to' US$15–35/hr; rates vary by assessment, location and project, and onboarding phases may pay less
Many reports of 'empty queue' periods and silent removal from projects; a 2026 blog reports large contributor cuts
Contractor work: no benefits, no guaranteed hours, you handle your own taxes
Scale AI faced 2024–25 California lawsuits alleging misclassification and unpaid training time (outcome not verified)
VPN use to hide your location is prohibited; eligibility differs by project

training.notes: Project onboarding against written guidelines; postings say lower rates may apply during onboarding. Whether screening time is paid was not evidenced.

compensation.notes: Official Outlier generalist listings that include Canada show 'up to' rates: US$15/hr (English writing/content review), US$18/hr (AI Evaluator – English), US$35/hr (general inbound). Specialist roles are higher (e.g. up to US$150/hr quant finance). A Built In mirror of a Canadian English writing posting cites an average of about US$25/hr.

reliability.notes: Third-party guides and forum posts describe empty queues when projects end and silent removals; a blog reports thousands removed around early 2026 and another references a Sept 2026 removal wave on one project. Anecdotal.

applicationSteps: Create an Outlier account and pick a listed opportunity that includes Canada
Complete the skills screening for that project
Set up a payout method (PayPal, Airtm or ACH per the FAQ)
Complete project onboarding and wait to be matched to tasks
fitsIf: You write clearly, follow detailed rules, and want flexible side income that can stop without notice.
notFitIf: You need steady, predictable hours or income you can budget around.

name: Accessibility tester with lived disability experience (Fable)
summary: Toronto-founded company that pays people with disabilities who use assistive technology to test websites and apps for accessibility.
whatYouDo: You complete testing tasks on client websites and apps using the assistive technology you already rely on (e.g. screen reader, magnification, alternative input) and give feedback. You choose how much to work each month.
appeal: Residents of Canada, the US and the UK are eligible (official)
Values lived experience with assistive technology over formal credentials
Paid training and a 'competitive hourly wage'; Fable says testers average more than double minimum wage
Credible: a Government of Canada notice named Fable as the only provider of this kind of tester pool
watchOuts: Only for adults with vision, mobility or cognitive accessibility needs, including daily assistive-technology users
Exact hourly rate not published in what we saw
Contractor status, paid once a month in arrears
Onboarding includes an assistive-technology and communication-skills assessment and a conversation with staff
Monthly work volume not published

training.notes: Testers complete paid training after the assessment.

compensation.notes: Fable describes a 'competitive hourly wage' and says testers earn on average more than double minimum wage; no figure published in what we saw. Paid at month-end.

reliability.notes: Testers choose how much to work monthly; available volume not published. A 2020 figure cited about 100 testers.

applicationSteps: Sign up on Fable's community page and verify your email
Describe the assistive technology you use
Talk with a Fable team member and complete the AT and communication skills assessment
Complete paid training, then take testing tasks
fitsIf: You are an experienced assistive-technology user in Canada who wants flexible, fairly paid remote work using that expertise.
notFitIf: You do not use assistive technology or need guaranteed monthly hours.

name: AI response evaluation and rating (category)
summary: Remote gig work rating, ranking and rewriting chatbot or search outputs so AI companies can improve their models.
whatYouDo: Typical tasks include reading two AI answers and choosing which better follows instructions, rewriting a weak answer, or rating search and content results against long guidelines. Work comes in project batches through platforms or vendors and is paid per hour or per task.
appeal: Fully remote with flexible hours on most platforms
Several platforms and vendors recruit Canada residents specifically
Strong writers and subject experts can earn well above minimum wage on some projects
Low barrier to try: most platforms are free to join
watchOuts: Journalism describes the work as often underpaid, sporadic and precarious, with no benefits
Hours are rarely guaranteed and projects can end without notice
Screening tests and onboarding are often unpaid
Fake job offers imitate real platforms; legitimate ones do not charge you to join
Pay is usually quoted in US dollars and you are typically an independent contractor

training.notes: Platforms typically require guideline study and qualification tests.

compensation.notes: Varies widely. Records in this file range from ~US$13.50/hr (TELUS est.) to US$50–70/hr (Mercor generalist) and more for specialists; the Globe and Mail profiled a rater at ~US$14/hr.

reliability.notes: Globe and Mail (2023) interviews describe sporadic, per-task work; 2026 blogs describe project cuts and empty queues.

applicationSteps: Shortlist legitimate platforms that accept Canada residents
Apply and complete the qualification test(s)
Set up a payout account (often PayPal or similar)
Keep more than one platform active because tasks come and go
fitsIf: You read carefully, write well, and want flexible remote side income you can scale up or down.
notFitIf: You need stable hours, benefits, or a predictable paycheque.
